newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma City bombing trial begins.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma City bombing trial begins.

text.p: The trial of Gulf War veteran Timothy McVeigh, accused of blowing up the Oklahoma City federal building in the worst attack against civilians in U.S. history, began on Monday.
U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch called the trial to order with an explanation of the jury selection process.
McVeigh and former army buddy Terry Nichols have been charged with bombing the Alfred P. Murrah federal building on April 19, 1995. The blast killed 168 people, including 19 children.
McVeigh and Nichols, who have both pleaded not guilty, are being tried separately. Nichols will be tried at a later date. The trial was moved to Denver to ensure a fair hearing.
"The defendant is present and ready and seated with me at this table," McVeigh's chief attorney Stephen Jones told the court. Nichols was not in the courtroom and is not expected to attend the trial.
Twelve seats in the courtroom were set aside for relatives of the victims and others injured in the bombing.
